hook.text: Japanese hiragana has a symbol for 'ka,' another for 'ki,' another for 'ku'—each covers a whole syllable.

buildup.text: A syllabary has one symbol per syllable—not per individual sound.

discovery.text: Cherokee's syllabary was invented by Sequoyah in the 1820s—literacy spread in just a few years.

twist.text: Syllabaries work best for languages with simple syllable structures—Japanese 'ka-ki-ku' fits perfectly.

climax.text: Languages with complex consonant clusters would need thousands of symbols—making syllabaries impractical.

punchline.text: One symbol per syllable—simple, elegant, but size-limited.

quiz.question: What does each symbol in a syllabary represent?
